# Parameters and setup {#sec-parameters}

Everything that can be tuned lives in this one chunk. Nothing below re-defines a
parameter; downstream code only reads them.

The one structural change versus `sensitivity_analysis_2026_07_17_v11.R`:
**the gate and the pool are now always driven by the objective, equal-weight
overall score.** Consumer or scenario weights only re-score the candidates that
have already cleared that shared floor. The old "full personalization" mode
(gate + pool + selection all on the personal score) is no longer the default
anywhere; it survives only as an explicit comparison in @sec-personalization.

```{r}
#| label: parameters

## ========================================================================== #
## 1.1  Core parameters ====
## ========================================================================== #

# --- Normalization -----------------------------------------------------------
# PRIMARY profile: drives every algorithm run and every result in sections 3-7
# and 9. Section 8 compares profiles against each other regardless of this value.
# Candidates: "initial", "minmax_pct", "log_tails", "log_tails_TL",
#             "zscore", "rank", "log_EAWS", "log_EAWS_TL"
norm_profile <- "log_tails"

# Offset used inside the log transform (AW & SE).
#   "absolute"        : the same raw-unit constant for both dimensions
#   "relative_median" : a fixed FRACTION of each dimension's own median nonzero
#                       raw value -- avoids the AW/SE scale asymmetry
LOG_OFFSET_MODE  <- "relative_median"
LOG_OFFSET_VALUE <- 1

# --- Substitutability --------------------------------------------------------
# 5 = perfect substitutes only (strictest); 3 = loosest.
SUBST_LEVELS           <- c(3, 4, 5)
substitutability_level <- 4          # the level used for all single-level results

# --- Gate / pool -------------------------------------------------------------
GATE_THRESHOLD <- 0.80   # reference score >= this  -> "good enough", no recommendation
POOL_THRESHOLD <- 0.75   # only used when POOL_MODE == "absolute"
# GATE_MODE: what "good enough, no recommendation needed" means
#   "overall"        : the single equal-weight overall score >= GATE_THRESHOLD   <-- default
#   "all_dimensions" : EVERY one of E, AW, SE, H >= GATE_THRESHOLD individually.
#                      A product with three dimensions at 0.95 and one at 0.40
#                      is "good enough" under "overall" (its average clears 0.75)
#                      but gated under "all_dimensions" (that one weak dimension
#                      triggers a search for an alternative). Candidate ranking
#                      and pool eligibility (POOL_MODE) are unaffected either way
#                      - only whether the reference itself needs a recommendation
#                      changes. Compared head-to-head in @sec-gatemode.
GATE_MODE <- "overall"
# POOL_MODE: how a candidate becomes eligible
#   "absolute"       : score >= POOL_THRESHOLD (the original fixed 0.75 cut-off)
#   "beat_reference" : score > the reference's own score      <-- default
#   "none"           : every relevant product is eligible; softmax alone decides
POOL_MODE <- "beat_reference"

# Objective weights: used for the overall score that drives BOTH gate and pool
# in every run in this document. Order: E, AW, SE, H.
ALGO_WEIGHTS <- c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25)

# --- Selection among eligible candidates -------------------------------------
RANDOMIZE   <- TRUE   # the app's behaviour; validation code overrides to FALSE
SHARPNESS   <- 15     # softmax temperature = 1/SHARPNESS. 0 = uniform draw.
RANDOM_SEED <- 42

# --- Theoretical weight grid (section 5) -------------------------------------
# Uniform simplex grid: every (E,AW,SE,H) multiple of the step summing to 1.
# 0.05 -> 1,771 vectors. (The Dirichlet and trimmed grids of v11 are dropped.)
WEIGHT_GRID_STEP <- 0.05

# --- Section 8: which normalization profiles to compare ----------------------
# Set to NULL for "all". Edit this vector to include/exclude profiles.
PROFILES_TO_COMPARE <- NULL

# --- Worked basket example (section 5.7) -------------------------------------
# Everyday products used to illustrate what a shopper actually sees. Codes that
# do not exist in the current database are silently skipped. Resolved by exact
# food_product name match against the database (22 items requested):
#   Pork loin / Beef minced steak 15% / Chicken meat / Milk semi-skimmed UHT /
#   Emmental / Butter 80% / Baguette / Sugar / Sunflower oil / Olive oil extra
#   virgin / Potato peeled / Orange pulp / Apple pulp / Tap water / Coffee
#   ready-to-drink / Beer regular / Shepherd's pie / Liquid cream 30% / Cashew
#   nut / Salmon farmed / Chocolate cake / Egg powder.
BASKET_TH <- c("TH1594", "TH1514", "TH1709", "TH1996", "TH1872", "TH0046",
               "TH0855", "TH2249", "TH0097", "TH0090", "TH2171", "TH0728",
               "TH0787", "TH0427", "TH2035", "TH0009", "TH0323", "TH1963",
               "TH1404", "TH0580", "TH1017", "TH0440")

# --- I/O ---------------------------------------------------------------------
path_db     <- "data_raw/TH_WP3-FULL DATABASE-v2026-07-14.csv"
path_matrix <- "data_raw/Step1_encoding_v2026-05-28.csv"
path_xlsx   <- "data_raw/RawData.xlsx"        # five-country consumer survey

HAS_CONSUMERS   <- file.exists(here::here(path_xlsx))   # section 6 runs only if present
MAKE_PLOTS      <- TRUE
FORCE_RECOMPUTE <- TRUE   # TRUE = ignore the cache and recompute everything

# The cache is keyed on parameters and input files, NOT on the code inside a
# cached block. If you edit the body of a cached() call, bump this string (or set
# FORCE_RECOMPUTE) or you will silently keep reading the old result.
CACHE_VERSION <- "v12.0" 

dim_cols <- c("E", "AW", "SE", "H")           # canonical dimension order
stopifnot(substitutability_level %in% SUBST_LEVELS)
```

```{r}
## 1.2  Libraries, folders and small helpers ====

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(here); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2)
})
options(width = 110)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 10))

for (d in c("output", "cache")) if (!dir.exists(here(d))) dir.create(here(d), recursive = TRUE)

# --- Table printer: kableExtra if available, plain kable otherwise ------------
show_tbl <- function(df, caption = NULL, digits = 3, full_width = FALSE) {
  df <- as.data.frame(df)
  k  <- knitr::kable(df, caption = caption, digits = digits, row.names = FALSE)
  if (requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE)) {
    k <- tryCatch({
      kk <- kableExtra::kable_styling(
        k, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
        full_width = full_width, font_size = 12, position = "left")
      if (nrow(df) > 25) kk <- tryCatch(kableExtra::scroll_box(kk, height = "520px"),
                                        error = function(e) kk)
      kk
    }, error = function(e) k)
  }
  k
}

# --- Caching -----------------------------------------------------------------
# cached(key, fingerprint, expr): reuse a cached result unless the fingerprint
# changed or FORCE_RECOMPUTE is TRUE. expr is lazy: only evaluated on a miss.
cached <- function(key, fingerprint, expr) {
  fingerprint <- c(fingerprint, CACHE_VERSION)     # bumping CACHE_VERSION invalidates all
  fp   <- substr(paste(as.character(fingerprint), collapse = "|"), 1, 4000)
  tag  <- abs(sum(utf8ToInt(fp)) * 31L + nchar(fp))
  path <- here("cache", sprintf("%s__%d.rds", key, tag))
  if (!FORCE_RECOMPUTE && file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  val <- eval.parent(substitute(expr))
  saveRDS(val, path); val
}
file_fp <- function(p) if (file.exists(p)) {
  fi <- file.info(p); paste(fi$size, as.numeric(fi$mtime))
} else "missing"

# --- Statistics --------------------------------------------------------------
skewness <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]; n <- length(x); s <- sd(x)
  if (n < 3 || s == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (sum((x - mean(x))^3) / n) / s^3
}
eta_sq <- function(x, g) {                      # between-group variance share
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(g); x <- x[ok]; g <- as.factor(g[ok])
  if (length(x) < 3) return(NA_real_)
  grand <- mean(x); ss_tot <- sum((x - grand)^2)
  if (ss_tot == 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(tapply(x, g, function(v) length(v) * (mean(v) - grand)^2)) / ss_tot
}
jacc <- function(a, b) if (length(a) == 0 && length(b) == 0) NA_real_ else
  length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))

# --- Artifact register -------------------------------------------------------
# Every file this document writes is registered here and listed in the appendix,
# so there is one place to see what exists on disk.
.ARTIFACTS <- new.env(parent = emptyenv()); .ARTIFACTS$rows <- list()
register_out <- function(file, what) {
  .ARTIFACTS$rows[[length(.ARTIFACTS$rows) + 1]] <-
    data.frame(file = file, contents = what, row.names = NULL); invisible(NULL)
}
save_out <- function(x, file, what) {
  utils::write.csv(x, here("output", file), row.names = FALSE)
  register_out(file, what); invisible(x)
}
```

## Raw dimension scores

Higher raw value = **worse** (an impact / risk score) on all four dimensions.
Normalization flips them so that higher = better.

## Normalization profiles

```{r}
#| label: normalization

## ========================================================================== #
## 2.3  Normalization: one transform per dimension, bundled into profiles ====
## ========================================================================== #
# norm_one_dim() maps a raw IMPACT vector (higher = worse) to a GOODNESS score
# (higher = better).
#   minmax_whisker : global min; max = largest Tukey top-whisker across L1 cats
#   minmax_p       : min-max anchored at the 1st/99th percentile, clamped
#   log_minmax_p   : log(x + offset) first, THEN percentile min-max
#   zscore         : standardise then flip sign (unbounded)
#   rank           : percentile rank then flip (discards magnitude)

norm_one_dim <- function(impact, method, l1 = NULL, p_lo = 0.01, p_hi = 0.99) {
  x <- impact; ok <- !is.na(x)

  if (method == "minmax_whisker") {
    thr <- data.frame(x = x, g = l1) %>% filter(!is.na(x)) %>% group_by(g) %>%
      summarise(Q3 = quantile(x, .75), IQR = IQR(x),
                tw = max(x[x <= Q3 + 1.5 * IQR]), .groups = "drop")
    max_val <- max(thr$tw, na.rm = TRUE); min_val <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    return(pmax(1 - (x - min_val) / (max_val - min_val), 0))
  }
  if (method == "log_minmax_p") {
    o <- if (LOG_OFFSET_MODE == "relative_median")
           LOG_OFFSET_VALUE * median(x[x > 0], na.rm = TRUE) else LOG_OFFSET_VALUE
    x <- log(pmax(x, 0) + o)
  }
  if (method %in% c("minmax_p", "log_minmax_p")) {
    lo <- as.numeric(quantile(x, p_lo, na.rm = TRUE))
    hi <- as.numeric(quantile(x, p_hi, na.rm = TRUE))
    return(1 - pmin(pmax((x - lo) / (hi - lo), 0), 1))
  }
  if (method == "zscore") return(-(x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  if (method == "rank")
    return(1 - (rank(x, na.last = "keep", ties.method = "average") - 1) / (sum(ok) - 1))
  stop("Unknown normalization method: ", method)
}

# A profile is a per-dimension choice of method. H = "letters" uses the A-E map.
norm_profiles <- list(
  initial      = list(E = "minmax_whisker", AW = "minmax_whisker", SE = "minmax_whisker", H = "letters"),
  minmax_pct   = list(E = "minmax_p",       AW = "minmax_p",       SE = "minmax_p",       H = "minmax_p"),
  log_tails    = list(E = "minmax_p",       AW = "log_minmax_p",   SE = "log_minmax_p",   H = "minmax_p"),
  log_tails_TL = list(E = "minmax_whisker", AW = "log_minmax_p",   SE = "log_minmax_p",   H = "minmax_p"),
  log_EAWS     = list(E = "log_minmax_p",   AW = "log_minmax_p",   SE = "log_minmax_p",   H = "minmax_p"),
  log_EAWS_TL  = list(E = "log_minmax_p",   AW = "log_minmax_p",   SE = "log_minmax_p",   H = "letters"),
  zscore       = list(E = "zscore",         AW = "zscore",         SE = "zscore",         H = "zscore"),
  rank         = list(E = "rank",           AW = "rank",           SE = "rank",           H = "rank")
)

build_norm_matrix <- function(db, profile) {
  m <- cbind(
    E  = norm_one_dim(db$E_SS,  profile$E,  db$SAFAD_L1_cat),
    AW = norm_one_dim(db$AW_SS, profile$AW, db$SAFAD_L1_cat),
    SE = norm_one_dim(db$SE_SS, profile$SE, db$SAFAD_L1_cat),
    H  = if (profile$H == "letters") db$H_letter_goodness
         else norm_one_dim(db$H_SS, profile$H, db$SAFAD_L1_cat))
  rownames(m) <- NULL; m
}

weight_archetypes <- list(
  Equal        = c(.25, .25, .25, .25), `Env-heavy`    = c(.55, .15, .15, .15),
  `AW-heavy`   = c(.15, .55, .15, .15), `SE-heavy`     = c(.15, .15, .55, .15),
  `Health-heavy` = c(.15, .15, .15, .55))
```

## The algorithm {#sec-algo}

One function, one code path. The design point that matters for everything below:

* **`gp_score`** (gate/pool score) decides *who gets a recommendation* and
  *which candidates are eligible*. In this document it is **always** the
  objective equal-weight overall score.
* **`select_mat %*% w`** decides *which* of the eligible candidates is shown.
  This is the only place personal weights act.

Because `gp_score` no longer depends on the weights, **eligibility can be
computed once and reused** for all 1,771 grid vectors and all ~2,800
respondents. That is what makes the big runs in @sec-runs cheap, and it also
means coverage (who is gated, who is served) is *identical* across all weight
vectors — only the identity of the recommended product changes.

```{r}
#| label: algorithm

## ========================================================================== #
## 2.4  Eligibility, selection, and the user-facing run_algo() ====
## ========================================================================== #

# ---- Step 1: eligibility (weight-independent when gp_score is objective) ----
# Returns, per product: its eligible candidate set and the outcome reason.
#   good_enough    : reference already >= gate            -> alternative = itself
#   no_alternative : gated, but nothing relevant qualifies -> alternative = itself
#   recommended    : a real alternative exists
build_eligibility <- function(gp_score, compat, ref_cat, gate_thr, pool_thr,
                              pool_mode = POOL_MODE, dim_mat = NULL, gate_mode = GATE_MODE) {
  n <- length(gp_score)
  cand <- vector("list", n); reason <- character(n)
  if (gate_mode == "all_dimensions" && is.null(dim_mat))
    stop("gate_mode = 'all_dimensions' requires dim_mat (the per-dimension score matrix)")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    s <- gp_score[i]
    if (is.na(s)) { cand[[i]] <- integer(0); reason[i] <- "no_score"; next }
    if (gate_mode == "all_dimensions") {
      if (anyNA(dim_mat[i, ])) { cand[[i]] <- integer(0); reason[i] <- "no_score"; next }
      good_enough <- all(dim_mat[i, ] >= gate_thr)
    } else {
      good_enough <- s >= gate_thr
    }
    if (good_enough) { cand[[i]] <- integer(0); reason[i] <- "good_enough"; next }
    pool <- compat[[ ref_cat[i] ]]; if (is.null(pool)) pool <- integer(0)
    pool <- pool[pool != i]
    ok   <- !is.na(gp_score[pool])
    cc <- if (pool_mode == "none")                pool[ok]
          else if (pool_mode == "beat_reference") pool[ok & gp_score[pool] > s]
          else                                    pool[ok & gp_score[pool] >= pool_thr]
    if (length(cc) == 0) { cand[[i]] <- integer(0); reason[i] <- "no_alternative" }
    else                 { cand[[i]] <- cc;         reason[i] <- "recommended"    }
  }
  gated <- if (gate_mode == "all_dimensions")
    !is.na(gp_score) & !apply(dim_mat, 1, function(r) !anyNA(r) && all(r >= gate_thr))
  else !is.na(gp_score) & gp_score < gate_thr
  list(cand = cand, reason = reason, gated = gated, served = reason == "recommended")
}

# ---- Step 2: selection, vectorised over MANY weight vectors at once ---------
# W = K x 4 matrix of weight vectors. Returns an n x K integer matrix of chosen
# alternative row ids (self when not served).
# Randomized draws use the Gumbel-max trick, which is an exact sample from the
# softmax over sharpness * score -- identical in distribution to v11's per-product
# `sample(prob = softmax)`, but vectorised. (v11 re-seeded per product; here the
# stream is seeded once per call, so individual draws differ while the
# distribution and the reproducibility guarantee do not.)
pick_alternatives <- function(elig, select_mat, W, randomize = FALSE,
                              seed = RANDOM_SEED, sharpness = 0) {
  W <- as.matrix(W); if (ncol(W) != 4L) stop("W must be K x 4 (E, AW, SE, H)")
  n <- length(elig$cand); K <- nrow(W)
  alt <- matrix(rep.int(seq_len(n), K), nrow = n, ncol = K)   # default: itself
  set.seed(seed)
  tW <- t(W)
  for (i in which(elig$served)) {
    cc <- elig$cand[[i]]; m <- length(cc)
    S  <- select_mat[cc, , drop = FALSE] %*% tW               # m x K
    if (randomize && m > 1) {
      U <- matrix(stats::runif(m * K), m, K)
      S <- if (sharpness > 0) sharpness * S - log(-log(U)) else U
    }
    alt[i, ] <- cc[max.col(t(S), ties.method = "first")]
  }
  alt
}

# ---- Step 3: the single-weight-vector wrapper -------------------------------
# Same signature and semantics as v11's run_gated_algo(), but built on the two
# functions above so there is only one implementation to trust.
run_algo <- function(gp_score, compat, ref_cat, gate_thr, pool_thr,
                     randomize = FALSE, seed = RANDOM_SEED, sharpness = 0,
                     select_mat = NULL, select_weights = NULL,
                     pool_mode = POOL_MODE, elig = NULL,
                     dim_mat = NULL, gate_mode = GATE_MODE) {
  if (is.null(elig))
    elig <- build_eligibility(gp_score, compat, ref_cat, gate_thr, pool_thr, pool_mode,
                              dim_mat = dim_mat, gate_mode = gate_mode)
  personalize <- !is.null(select_mat) && !is.null(select_weights)
  sm <- if (personalize) select_mat else cbind(gp_score, 0, 0, 0)
  w  <- if (personalize) matrix(select_weights, nrow = 1) else matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 1)
  alt <- pick_alternatives(elig, sm, w, randomize, seed, sharpness)[, 1]
  out <- data.frame(
    row_id = seq_along(gp_score), TH_code = DB$TH_code, food_product = DB$food_product,
    SAFAD_L1_cat = DB$SAFAD_L1_cat, SAFAD_L2_cat = ref_cat,
    overall_score = round(gp_score, 4), gated = elig$gated,
    alt_row_id = alt, alt_TH_code = DB$TH_code[alt], alt_product = DB$food_product[alt],
    alt_overall = round(gp_score[alt], 4), alt_is_self = alt == seq_along(gp_score),
    alt_reason = elig$reason,
    gain = round(gp_score[alt] - gp_score, 4),        # objective gain
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (personalize) {
    ps <- as.numeric(select_mat %*% as.numeric(select_weights))
    out$gain_personal <- round(ps[alt] - ps, 4)       # gain on the consumer's own score
  }
  out
}
```

## Relevance sets

```{r}
#| label: relevance-sets

## ========================================================================== #
## 2.5  Relevance (substitutability) sets, one per level ====
## ========================================================================== #
# compat_by_level[["L4"]][[cat]] = row indices of products that are acceptable
# alternatives for category `cat` at level 4 (i.e. matrix_A entry in {4, 5}).
cats_present <- intersect(unique(DB$SAFAD_L2_cat), colnames(matrix_A))
ref_cat_vec  <- DB$SAFAD_L2_cat

compat_by_level <- cached(
  paste0("compat_", paste(SUBST_LEVELS, collapse = ""), "_", n_all),
  c(SUBST_LEVELS, n_all, file_fp(here(path_matrix))), {
  setNames(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L) {
    codes <- as.character(L:5)
    setNames(lapply(cats_present, function(cc) {
      rel <- rownames(matrix_A)[matrix_A[, cc] %in% codes]
      which(DB$SAFAD_L2_cat %in% rel)
    }), cats_present)
  }), paste0("L", SUBST_LEVELS))
})

bind_rows(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L) {
  s <- lengths(compat_by_level[[paste0("L", L)]])
  data.frame(level = L, n_categories = length(s), min_pool = min(s),
             median_pool = as.integer(median(s)), max_pool = max(s))
})) %>% show_tbl(caption = "Size of the relevant-alternatives pool, by substitutability level.")
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Every diagonal entry of `matrix_A` is 5, so every L2 category is always a
substitute for itself. A product's pool therefore always contains its own
subcategory, and the effective decision problem is at the level of the 124
subcategories rather than the 2,451 products.
:::

# Raw data diagnostics {#sec-raw}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Run used:** none. Everything here is on the raw impact scale, before any
normalization or any algorithm.
:::

## Skewness

Why this matters: a long right tail is exactly what makes plain min-max
compress a dimension. A handful of extreme products pin the top of the scale and
everything else is squashed toward one end — the reason AW and SE get a log
transform in the primary profile.

```{r}
#| label: raw-skewness
data.frame(
  dimension = dim_cols,
  min    = sapply(RAW_IMPACT, function(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  median = sapply(RAW_IMPACT, function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  max    = sapply(RAW_IMPACT, function(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  skewness = sapply(RAW_IMPACT, skewness),
  pct_zero_or_negative = sapply(RAW_IMPACT, function(x) 100 * mean(x <= 0, na.rm = TRUE))
) %>% show_tbl(caption = "Raw impact distribution per dimension (higher = worse).", digits = 2)
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Note the last column, which matters again in @sec-relgain: **AW is zero for every
plant-based product (~41% of the catalogue) and H (the FNS score) is negative for
~29%.** Any metric that divides by a raw impact is therefore undefined or
sign-flipped for a large, non-random part of the database.
:::

## Correlations between raw dimensions

Spearman is invariant to any monotone per-dimension normalization, so the
Spearman block below is what survives into every bounded profile unchanged.
Pearson is what the log transform actually alters.

```{r}
#| label: raw-correlations
.pear  <- cor(RAW_IMPACT, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
.spear <- cor(RAW_IMPACT, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
raw_corr <- .pear; raw_corr[upper.tri(raw_corr)] <- .spear[upper.tri(.spear)]
raw_corr_tbl <- cbind(dimension = rownames(raw_corr), as.data.frame(round(raw_corr, 3)))
save_out(raw_corr_tbl, "raw_dimension_correlations.csv",
         "Raw-scale correlations: Pearson below the diagonal, Spearman above.")
show_tbl(raw_corr_tbl,
         caption = "Raw dimension correlations. Lower triangle = Pearson, upper = Spearman.")
```

## Raw dimension pairs

```{r}
#| label: fig-raw-pairs
#| fig-cap: "All six raw dimension pairs. Each facet header names the x and y dimension."
#| fig-height: 7
prs <- combn(dim_cols, 2, simplify = FALSE)
bind_rows(lapply(prs, function(p) data.frame(
  pair = paste0("x = ", p[1], "   |   y = ", p[2]),
  x = RAW_IMPACT[[p[1]]], y = RAW_IMPACT[[p[2]]]))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) + geom_point(size = .4, alpha = .25) +
  facet_wrap(~ pair, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Raw dimension pairs (impact scale, higher = worse)",
       x = "x-axis dimension (see facet header)", y = "y-axis dimension (see facet header)")
```

## Raw impact by dimension and food category

```{r}
#| label: fig-raw-boxplots
#| fig-cap: "Raw impact per L1 food category, one panel per dimension. Free x scales — the four dimensions are on completely different units and cannot be compared across panels."
#| fig-height: 9
raw_long <- data.frame(L1 = l1cat, RAW_IMPACT) %>%
  pivot_longer(-L1, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "impact") %>%
  filter(!is.na(impact)) %>%
  mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols),
         L1 = factor(L1, levels = rev(sort(unique(L1)))))
ggplot(raw_long, aes(impact, L1, fill = dimension)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .35, alpha = .8, linewidth = .3) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +

  labs(title = "Raw impact by L1 category and dimension",
       subtitle = "(lower score = more sustainable)",
       x = "Raw impact score (different scale per panel – reversed axes)", y = NULL) +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

# Core algorithm runs {#sec-runs}

Everything in @sec-theoretical through @sec-sweeps is extracted from a small
number of objects built here. Nothing downstream re-runs the algorithm except
@sec-sweeps, which is explicitly about varying the parameters.

| Object | What it is | Weights | Levels | Selection |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SCORES` | 4 normalized dimension scores + overall, for every product, under every normalization profile | equal | — | — |
| `REC` | the recommendation table — one row per product, one column block per level | equal (objective) | 3, 4, 5 | randomized, sharpness `r SHARPNESS` |
| `GRID` | the algorithm re-run for all 1,771 theoretical weight vectors | 1,771-vector simplex grid | 3, 4, 5 | deterministic best-in-pool |
| `CONS` | the algorithm re-run per survey respondent (@sec-consumers) | ~2,800 real weight vectors | primary only | randomized, sharpness `r SHARPNESS` |

In **all four**, the gate and the pool run on the objective equal-weight score.

## `SCORES` — normalized scores under every profile

```{r}
#| label: build-scores

## ========================================================================== #
## 4.1  SCORES: normalized dimension scores + overall, per profile ====
## ========================================================================== #
NORM <- lapply(norm_profiles, function(p) {
  m <- build_norm_matrix(DB, p); colnames(m) <- dim_cols; m
})
OVERALL_BY_PROFILE <- lapply(NORM, function(m) as.numeric(m %*% ALGO_WEIGHTS))

SCORES <- bind_rows(lapply(names(NORM), function(pn) {
  data.frame(row_id = seq_len(n_all), TH_code = DB$TH_code, food_product = DB$food_product,
             SAFAD_L1_cat = l1cat, SAFAD_L2_cat = subcat, profile = pn,
             NORM[[pn]], overall = OVERALL_BY_PROFILE[[pn]],
             check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}))
save_out(SCORES, "CORE_scores_by_profile.csv",
         "CORE 1/4. Per product x normalization profile: E, AW, SE, H and the equal-weight overall score.")

# Handles for the primary profile, used everywhere downstream.
select_mat_primary <- NORM[[norm_profile]]
overall_primary    <- OVERALL_BY_PROFILE[[norm_profile]]

cat(sprintf("SCORES: %d rows = %d products x %d profiles. Primary profile = '%s'.\n",
            nrow(SCORES), n_all, length(NORM), norm_profile))
```

## `REC` — the recommendation table (equal weights, three levels)

```{r}
#| label: build-rec

## ========================================================================== #
## 4.2  REC: the objective recommendation table, one column block per level ====
## ========================================================================== #
ELIG <- setNames(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L)
  build_eligibility(overall_primary, compat_by_level[[paste0("L", L)]],
                    ref_cat_vec, GATE_THRESHOLD, POOL_THRESHOLD, POOL_MODE,
                    dim_mat = select_mat_primary, gate_mode = GATE_MODE)),
  paste0("L", SUBST_LEVELS))
cat("Gate mode in effect for REC / GRID / CONS:", GATE_MODE, "\n")

algo_by_level <- setNames(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L)
  run_algo(overall_primary, compat_by_level[[paste0("L", L)]], ref_cat_vec,
           GATE_THRESHOLD, POOL_THRESHOLD, randomize = RANDOMIZE, seed = RANDOM_SEED,
           sharpness = SHARPNESS, elig = ELIG[[paste0("L", L)]])),
  paste0("L", SUBST_LEVELS))

REC <- algo_by_level[[1]][, c("row_id", "TH_code", "food_product",
                              "SAFAD_L1_cat", "SAFAD_L2_cat", "overall_score", "gated")]
for (L in SUBST_LEVELS) {
  a <- algo_by_level[[paste0("L", L)]]
  REC[[paste0("alt_TH_L", L)]]      <- a$alt_TH_code
  REC[[paste0("alt_product_L", L)]] <- a$alt_product
  REC[[paste0("alt_reason_L", L)]]  <- a$alt_reason
  REC[[paste0("alt_row_id_L", L)]]  <- a$alt_row_id
  REC[[paste0("gain_L", L)]]        <- a$gain
}
save_out(REC, "CORE_recommendations_by_level.csv",
         paste0("CORE 2/4. Equal-weight recommendations at levels ",
                paste(SUBST_LEVELS, collapse = "/"), ", profile ", norm_profile, "."))

bind_rows(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L) {
  a <- algo_by_level[[paste0("L", L)]]; ng <- sum(a$gated)
  data.frame(level = L,
             pct_gated          = round(100 * mean(a$gated), 1),
             pct_good_enough    = round(100 * mean(a$alt_reason == "good_enough"), 1),
             pct_no_alternative = round(100 * mean(a$alt_reason == "no_alternative"), 1),
             pct_recommended    = round(100 * mean(a$alt_reason == "recommended"), 1),
             pct_gated_served   = round(100 * sum(a$alt_reason == "recommended") / max(ng, 1), 1),
             mean_gain          = round(mean(a$gain[a$alt_reason == "recommended"]), 3),
             distinct_alts      = length(unique(a$alt_row_id[a$alt_reason == "recommended"])))
})) %>% show_tbl(caption = "Algorithm behaviour by substitutability level (equal weights).")
```

`pct_gated` is identical at every level because the gate depends only on the
reference product's own score. What the level changes is whether a gated product
can *find* an alternative, and how good that alternative is.

## `GRID` — the 1,771-vector theoretical weight grid

```{r}
#| label: build-grid

## ========================================================================== #
## 4.3  GRID: every weight vector on the 0.05 simplex grid, all three levels ====
## ========================================================================== #
# The grid is UNIFORM over the simplex. Note that the marginal distribution of
# any single dimension's weight is then Beta(1,3): most vectors give a given
# dimension very little weight, and single-dimension dominance is rare because
# it requires the other three to be near zero simultaneously.
build_weight_grid <- function(step = WEIGHT_GRID_STEP) {
  N <- round(1 / step); rows <- list()
  for (a in 0:N) for (b in 0:(N - a)) for (cc in 0:(N - a - b))
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c(a, b, cc, N - a - b - cc) * step
  m <- do.call(rbind, rows); colnames(m) <- dim_cols; m
}
W_GRID <- build_weight_grid()

GRID <- cached(
  paste0("GRID_", norm_profile, "_step", WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, "_",
         paste(SUBST_LEVELS, collapse = ""), "_", POOL_MODE),
  c(norm_profile, WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, SUBST_LEVELS, POOL_MODE, GATE_THRESHOLD,
    POOL_THRESHOLD, ALGO_WEIGHTS, LOG_OFFSET_MODE, LOG_OFFSET_VALUE, GATE_MODE), {
  out <- list(W = W_GRID, served = list(), alt = list())
  for (L in SUBST_LEVELS) {
    e <- ELIG[[paste0("L", L)]]
    full <- pick_alternatives(e, select_mat_primary, W_GRID,
                              randomize = FALSE, seed = RANDOM_SEED)
    out$served[[paste0("L", L)]] <- which(e$served)
    out$alt[[paste0("L", L)]]    <- full[e$served, , drop = FALSE]   # n_served x 1771
  }
  out
})

# Dominant dimension of each weight vector (used for the heatmaps in section 5).
GRID$dominant <- dim_cols[max.col(GRID$W, ties.method = "first")]

data.frame(level = SUBST_LEVELS,
           n_weight_vectors = nrow(GRID$W),
           n_products_served = sapply(paste0("L", SUBST_LEVELS), function(k) length(GRID$served[[k]])),
           n_cells = sapply(paste0("L", SUBST_LEVELS), function(k) length(GRID$alt[[k]]))) %>%
  show_tbl(caption = "GRID dimensions: one chosen alternative per served product per weight vector.")

data.frame(dominant_dimension = names(table(GRID$dominant)),
           n_weight_vectors = as.integer(table(GRID$dominant)),
           pct = round(100 * as.numeric(table(GRID$dominant)) / nrow(GRID$W), 1)) %>%
  show_tbl(caption = "How the 1,771 grid vectors split by their highest-weighted dimension.")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Because eligibility is objective, `GRID$served` is the **same set of products for
every one of the 1,771 weight vectors**. The grid therefore isolates exactly one
thing: how the weights change *which* alternative is shown, holding coverage
fixed. That is a cleaner tailoring experiment than v11's full-personalization
battery, where coverage and choice moved at the same time.
:::

```{r}
#| label: grid-consistency-check
# Sanity check: the vectorised grid engine must reproduce run_algo() exactly for
# a single weight vector. If this ever fails, the fast path has drifted.
.k    <- which(apply(GRID$W, 1, function(r) all(abs(r - 0.25) < 1e-9)))[1]
.slow <- run_algo(overall_primary, compat_by_level[[paste0("L", substitutability_level)]],
                  ref_cat_vec, GATE_THRESHOLD, POOL_THRESHOLD, randomize = FALSE,
                  select_mat = select_mat_primary, select_weights = GRID$W[.k, ],
                  elig = ELIG[[paste0("L", substitutability_level)]])
.srv  <- GRID$served[[paste0("L", substitutability_level)]]
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(.slow$alt_row_id[.srv]),
                    as.integer(GRID$alt[[paste0("L", substitutability_level)]][, .k])))
cat("Consistency check passed: vectorised grid == run_algo() for the equal-weight vector.\n")
```

# Performance under theoretical weights {#sec-theoretical}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Run used:** `GRID` (1,771 weight vectors, deterministic best-in-pool, all three
levels) for everything about tailoring; `REC` (equal weights, randomized,
level `r substitutability_level`) for the before/after picture and the basket.
Gate and pool are objective in both.
:::

```{r}
#| label: sec5-handles
LKEY   <- paste0("L", substitutability_level)
SRV    <- GRID$served[[LKEY]]                      # row ids of served products
ALT    <- GRID$alt[[LKEY]]                         # n_served x 1771
K_GRID <- ncol(ALT)
cat(sprintf("Primary run: level %d, %d served products x %d weight vectors.\n",
            substitutability_level, length(SRV), K_GRID))
```

## Most-recommended alternatives per subcategory {#sec-top5}

For every L2 subcategory we count how often each product is served as the
alternative, pooling over (a) every reference product belonging to that
subcategory and (b) all 1,771 weight vectors. The top five per subcategory and
per level is the "what does this subcategory actually get pushed towards"
summary.

`share` is the percentage of all (reference × weight-vector) recommendations
issued for that subcategory that landed on this alternative.

```{r}
#| label: top5-by-subcat
top_alts_by_cat <- cached(
  paste0("top5_", norm_profile, "_step", WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, "_", POOL_MODE),
  c(norm_profile, WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, SUBST_LEVELS, POOL_MODE, GATE_THRESHOLD, GATE_MODE), {
  bind_rows(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L) {
    key <- paste0("L", L); srv <- GRID$served[[key]]; A <- GRID$alt[[key]]
    data.frame(SAFAD_L2_cat = rep(ref_cat_vec[srv], times = ncol(A)),
               alt_row_id   = as.vector(A)) %>%
      count(SAFAD_L2_cat, alt_row_id, name = "times") %>%
      group_by(SAFAD_L2_cat) %>%
      mutate(share = 100 * times / sum(times)) %>%
      slice_max(times, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(rank = row_number()) %>% ungroup() %>%
      transmute(level = L, SAFAD_L2_cat, rank,
                alt_TH_code = DB$TH_code[alt_row_id],
                alt_product = DB$food_product[alt_row_id],
                alt_L2_cat  = DB$SAFAD_L2_cat[alt_row_id],
                times, share = round(share, 1))
  }))
})

# Subcategories where nothing is ever recommended (every product clears the gate)
# are added explicitly so the table covers all 124, rather than silently dropping.
all_cats <- sort(unique(ref_cat_vec))
never_served <- bind_rows(lapply(SUBST_LEVELS, function(L) {
  miss <- setdiff(all_cats, top_alts_by_cat$SAFAD_L2_cat[top_alts_by_cat$level == L])
  if (!length(miss)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(level = L, SAFAD_L2_cat = miss, rank = NA_integer_,
             alt_TH_code = NA_character_, alt_product = "(no product in this subcategory is ever gated)",
             alt_L2_cat = NA_character_, times = 0L, share = NA_real_)
}))
top_alts_by_cat <- bind_rows(top_alts_by_cat, never_served) %>% arrange(level, SAFAD_L2_cat, rank)

save_out(top_alts_by_cat, "top5_alternatives_by_subcategory.csv",
         "Top-5 most-recommended alternatives per L2 subcategory, per substitutability level, over the 1,771-weight grid.")

cat(sprintf("%d rows = %d subcategories x %d levels, up to 5 alternatives each.\n",
            nrow(top_alts_by_cat), length(all_cats), length(SUBST_LEVELS)))
top_alts_by_cat %>% filter(level == substitutability_level) %>%
  select(-level) %>% head(60) %>%
  show_tbl(caption = paste0("Top-5 alternatives per subcategory at level ",
                            substitutability_level, " (first 60 rows; full table in output/)."))
```

### Most-recommended products overall

The subcategory view above answers "what does THIS subcategory get pushed
towards"; this collapses that same count across every subcategory at once, to
answer "which handful of products account for a disproportionate share of all
recommendations, catalogue-wide". A product dominating this list is either a
genuinely excellent all-rounder, or a signal that the pool for its category is
thin — worth cross-checking against @sec-distinct's `top_alt_share` column.

```{r}
#| label: top10-overall
top10_overall <- data.frame(
    SAFAD_L2_cat = rep(ref_cat_vec[SRV], times = ncol(ALT)),
    alt_row_id   = as.vector(ALT)) %>%
  count(alt_row_id, name = "times") %>%
  mutate(share = round(100 * times / sum(times), 2)) %>%
  slice_max(times, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  transmute(rank, alt_TH_code = DB$TH_code[alt_row_id], alt_product = DB$food_product[alt_row_id],
            alt_L1_cat = DB$SAFAD_L1_cat[alt_row_id], alt_L2_cat = DB$SAFAD_L2_cat[alt_row_id],
            times, share)
save_out(top10_overall, "top10_alternatives_overall.csv",
         "Top-10 most-recommended products catalogue-wide, over the 1,771-weight grid, primary level.")
show_tbl(top10_overall, caption = paste0("Top-10 most-recommended products overall, level ",
                                         substitutability_level, ", over the 1,771-weight grid."))
```

## Before vs. after, by dimension and L1 category {#sec-beforeafter}

::: {.callout-warning appearance="default"}
## Why categories were missing from this figure in v11

They were not dropped by a plotting bug. The v11 code built this figure from
`alt_reason == "recommended"` only, and in those categories **no product is ever
gated** — every one of them already scores above 0.75, so the algorithm
correctly leaves them alone and they contribute zero rows.

The table below is the check. With the current database and settings, **seven**
categories have zero served products, not four: on top of the four you spotted
(starchy roots and tubers, non-alcoholic beverages, fruit and vegetable juices,
food for infants and small children) there are also alcoholic beverages,
drinking water, and products for special nutritional use.

The fix is to plot **the whole catalogue** rather than only served products.
Every product contributes; those that are `good_enough` or `no_alternative`
simply have *after = before*. This is also the more honest figure for a paper:
it is the improvement the catalogue actually realises, not the improvement
conditional on having been served.
:::

```{r}
#| label: coverage-by-l1
coverage_L1 <- REC %>%
  transmute(L1 = SAFAD_L1_cat, reason = .data[[paste0("alt_reason_", LKEY)]]) %>%
  count(L1, reason) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = reason, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
for (cl in c("good_enough", "no_alternative", "recommended"))
  if (!cl %in% names(coverage_L1)) coverage_L1[[cl]] <- 0L
coverage_L1 <- coverage_L1 %>%
  mutate(n_products = good_enough + no_alternative + recommended,
         pct_recommended = round(100 * recommended / n_products, 1)) %>%
  arrange(pct_recommended)
save_out(coverage_L1, "coverage_by_L1_category.csv",
         "Per L1 category: how many products are good_enough / have no alternative / are served.")
show_tbl(coverage_L1, caption = paste0(
  "Why some categories carry no recommendations at level ", substitutability_level,
  ". Categories with pct_recommended = 0 were the ones absent from the v11 figure."))
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="default"}
