right as far as it went, but incomplete, and a second draft you sent — same
`log_tails` profile, same level 4, dated July 7 — makes that clear: the
normalization profile is held fixed between that draft and this one, yet the
shrinkage is still large. So the profile cannot be the (whole) story. It also
isn't the substitutability level: both drafts are explicitly titled "level 4".

The actual cause is a change **I** made to how the figure aggregates, not
anything about the algorithm or the data. The July drafts averaged
before/after **only over products that actually received a recommendation**
(`alt_reason == "recommended"`) — which is also exactly what the v11 code did,
as you can see in its section 5.4. My "whole catalogue" fix in the previous
message averaged over **every** product instead, so that categories with zero
recommendations would still appear (rather than silently vanishing, which was
the original v11 bug). That fix was correct for the *missing-categories*
problem, but it has a side effect I didn't flag: for a category where only,
say, 30% of products get swapped, the other 70% now contribute `after = before`
to the mean, diluting the visible movement by roughly that same 70%.

Verified, same run (log_tails, level 4, equal weights) — whole-catalogue mean
vs. served-only mean:

| category | dimension | % served | whole-catalogue Δ | served-only Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Milk and dairy products | E  | 56% | 0.075 | **0.134** |
| Milk and dairy products | AW | 56% | 0.154 | **0.274** |
| Eggs and egg products   | AW | 31% | 0.145 | **0.472** |
| Snacks, desserts, and other foods | AW | 11% | 0.012 | **0.106** |
| Meat and meat products  | AW | 96% | 0.640 | 0.667 |

The pattern is exactly what dilution predicts: where coverage is high (Meat, 96%
served) the two numbers are nearly identical, because there's almost nothing
left to dilute with. Where coverage is low (Snacks, 11% served) the
whole-catalogue number is a small fraction of the served-only one. Milk and
dairy's "barely any improvement" on E and AW was never true of the products
that actually get swapped — it was the average being pulled toward zero by the
44% of the category the algorithm correctly leaves alone.

**Fix below:** the figure now reports the served-only mean again (so real
swap sizes are visible), while still solving the original missing-categories
problem explicitly — a category with zero recommendations gets a flat grey
marker labelled as such, rather than either vanishing (the v11 bug) or being
diluted into a near-invisible line (my overcorrection last time). Each
category's label also states what fraction of it was actually served, and the
line's transparency scales with that same fraction, so a long, faint arrow
reads visually as "large gain, but based on few products" rather than looking
identical to a short, opaque one.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-before-after
#| fig-cap: "Mean normalized score before vs. after recommendation, among products that actually receive one, by dimension and L1 category. Categories with zero recommendations are shown as a flat grey marker. Line transparency scales with the share of the category that was served; red arrowheads mark decreases."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 13
alt_col    <- paste0("alt_row_id_", LKEY)
reason_col <- paste0("alt_reason_", LKEY)
served_mask <- REC[[reason_col]] == "recommended"

before_after_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(dim_cols, function(d) data.frame(
    L1 = REC$SAFAD_L1_cat, dimension = d,
    before = select_mat_primary[REC$row_id, d],
    after_if_served = select_mat_primary[REC[[alt_col]], d],   # = before itself when not served
    served = served_mask)))

before_after <- before_after_rows %>% group_by(dimension, L1) %>%
  summarise(n_products = n(), n_served = sum(served),
            before = if (any(served)) mean(before[served], na.rm = TRUE) else mean(before, na.rm = TRUE),
            after  = if (any(served)) mean(after_if_served[served], na.rm = TRUE) else mean(before, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(coverage_L1[, c("L1", "pct_recommended")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(delta = after - before,
         direction = dplyr::case_when(
           n_served == 0     ~ "no recommendations issued",
           delta < -1e-9     ~ "decrease",
           TRUE              ~ "increase"),
         dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols))

save_out(before_after, "before_after_by_dimension_L1_served_only.csv",
         "Mean normalized score before vs after recommendation, per dimension x L1 category, among SERVED products only (n_served = 0 rows have before = after by construction).")

l1_order <- coverage_L1 %>% arrange(pct_recommended) %>%
  mutate(lab = sprintf("%s (%.0f%% served)", L1, pct_recommended))
before_after <- before_after %>%
  left_join(l1_order[, c("L1", "lab")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(l1_order$lab)))

decreases <- before_after %>% filter(direction == "decrease") %>%
  select(dimension, L1, n_served, pct_recommended, before, after, delta) %>% arrange(delta)

ggplot(before_after) +
  geom_segment(data = ~ filter(.x, n_served > 0),
               aes(x = before, xend = after, y = lab, yend = lab,
                   colour = direction, alpha = pct_recommended),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = .6) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, n_served == 0),
             aes(before, lab), colour = "grey55", shape = 4, size = 1.6, stroke = .8) +
  geom_point(aes(before, lab), colour = "grey35", size = .9) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(decrease = "#c0392b", increase = "#2e8540",
                                `no recommendations issued` = "grey55"), name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), limits = c(0, 100), name = "% of category served") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  labs(title = paste0("Mean score before vs. after, among SERVED products, by L1 category (level ",
                      substitutability_level, ", equal weights)"),
       subtitle = "Grey x = category has zero recommendations (before = after trivially). Fainter arrow = based on a smaller share of the category.",
       x = "normalized goodness (higher = better)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-decreases
show_tbl(decreases, caption = "Dimension x L1 combinations where the SERVED-ONLY mean normalized score falls after recommendation.")
```

These are genuine trade-offs, not errors: the algorithm maximises the *overall*
equal-weight score, so it will accept a loss on one dimension when the other
three gain more.

### The same figure, averaged over the whole catalogue instead

This is the complementary view: every product contributes, with unserved
products (`good_enough` or `no_alternative`) counted as `after = before`. No
category can vanish here (that was the original v11 bug), but a category's
visible movement is now diluted in proportion to `1 - pct_recommended` — a
category where only 10% of products are swapped will look like it barely
changes, even if those swaps are individually large (compare to the served-only
version above, or to the `pct_recommended` column in each label). Read this
version when you want "how much does the catalogue move as a whole"; read the
served-only version above when you want "how big is a swap when one happens".

```{r}
#| label: fig-before-after-wholecat
#| fig-cap: "The same comparison, averaged over the WHOLE catalogue rather than served products only. Unserved products contribute after = before, so movement is diluted in proportion to how much of the category was actually touched."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 13
before_after_wholecat <- before_after_rows %>% group_by(dimension, L1) %>%
  summarise(before = mean(before, na.rm = TRUE), after = mean(after_if_served, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(coverage_L1[, c("L1", "pct_recommended")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(delta = after - before,
         direction = ifelse(delta < -1e-9, "decrease", "increase or unchanged"),
         dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols)) %>%
  left_join(l1_order[, c("L1", "lab")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(l1_order$lab)))

save_out(before_after_wholecat, "before_after_by_dimension_L1_whole_catalogue.csv",
         "Mean normalized score before vs after recommendation, per dimension x L1 category, over the WHOLE catalogue (unserved products contribute after = before).")

ggplot(before_after_wholecat) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = before, xend = after, y = lab, yend = lab, colour = direction),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = .5) +
  geom_point(aes(before, lab), colour = "grey35", size = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(decrease = "#c0392b", `increase or unchanged` = "#2e8540"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = paste0("Mean score before vs. after, WHOLE CATALOGUE, by L1 category (level ",
                      substitutability_level, ", equal weights)"),
       subtitle = "Every product contributes; unserved products have after = before by construction.",
       x = "normalized goodness (higher = better)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
```

### Breaking the average apart: one arrow per quartile instead of one per category

The whole-catalogue arrow above is a single mean, and a mean can hide a lot —
a category could move a little because everyone moves a little, or because a
quarter of it moves a lot while the rest doesn't move at all. This is the
Gantt-chart version: within **each category x dimension cell separately**,
products are split into four quartiles by their own reference score on that
dimension (Q1 = worst 25% on this dimension, Q4 = already the best 25%), and
each quartile gets its own before/after arrow, still computed the
whole-catalogue way (unserved products contribute `after = before`). Behind
each arrow, a coloured band shows the range of "before" scores actually inside
that quartile, and a fainter grey band behind that shows the full range for
the whole category x dimension cell, so you can see both how wide a quartile
is and how it sits inside the category as a whole.

```{r}
#| label: fig-before-after-quartile
#| fig-cap: "Whole-catalogue before/after, broken into one arrow per quartile per category (Q1 = worst 25% on that dimension, Q4 = best 25%). Coloured band = range of 'before' scores within the quartile; pale grey band = full category range on that dimension. Arrow transparency scales with the quartile's own share served."
#| fig-height: 24
#| fig-width: 14
quart_labels <- c("Q1 (worst 25%)", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 (best 25%)")

before_after_quartile <- before_after_rows %>%
  group_by(dimension, L1) %>%
  mutate(n_in_cell = n(),
         quartile = ifelse(n_in_cell >= 4, ntile(before, 4), NA_integer_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(quartile)) %>%
  group_by(dimension, L1, quartile) %>%
  summarise(n_products = n(), n_served = sum(served),
            before_mean = mean(before, na.rm = TRUE),
            after_mean  = mean(after_if_served, na.rm = TRUE),
            q_min = min(before, na.rm = TRUE), q_max = max(before, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_served = round(100 * n_served / n_products, 1),
         quart_label = factor(quart_labels[quartile], levels = quart_labels),
         direction = dplyr::case_when(
           n_served == 0 ~ "no recommendations issued",
           after_mean - before_mean < -1e-9 ~ "decrease",
           TRUE ~ "increase"))

cat(sprintf("%d of %d categories have at least 4 products per dimension and get a quartile breakdown; the rest are too small to split and are omitted from this figure only.\n",
            n_distinct(before_after_quartile$L1), length(unique(l1cat))))

cat_range <- before_after_rows %>% group_by(dimension, L1) %>%
  summarise(cat_min = min(before, na.rm = TRUE), cat_max = max(before, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Build one combined y-axis: each category's 4 quartile-rows kept adjacent, in
# the same category order as the averaged figure above (l1_order, by coverage).
quartile_levels <- unlist(lapply(l1_order$lab[l1_order$L1 %in% unique(before_after_quartile$L1)],
                                 function(L) paste0(L, "  |  ", quart_labels)))
before_after_quartile <- before_after_quartile %>%
  left_join(l1_order[, c("L1", "lab")], by = "L1") %>%
  left_join(cat_range, by = c("L1", "dimension")) %>%
  mutate(row_label = paste0(lab, "  |  ", quart_label),
         row_label = factor(row_label, levels = rev(quartile_levels)),
         y_pos = as.numeric(row_label))

save_out(before_after_quartile, "before_after_by_dimension_L1_quartile.csv",
         "Whole-catalogue before/after broken down by quartile of the reference product's own dimension score, per L1 category x dimension.")

n_rows <- nlevels(before_after_quartile$row_label)
ggplot(before_after_quartile) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = cat_min, xmax = cat_max, ymin = y_pos - 0.44, ymax = y_pos + 0.44),
            fill = "grey82", colour = NA) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = q_min, xmax = q_max, ymin = y_pos - 0.32, ymax = y_pos + 0.32, fill = quart_label),
            alpha = .55, colour = NA) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = before_mean, xend = after_mean, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos,
                   colour = direction, alpha = pct_served),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.08, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = .55) +
  geom_point(aes(before_mean, y_pos), colour = "grey15", size = .7) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_len(n_rows), labels = levels(before_after_quartile$row_label),
                     expand = expansion(add = 1)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu", name = "quartile (within category x dimension)") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(decrease = "#c0392b", increase = "#2e8540",
                                `no recommendations issued` = "grey55"), name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.3, 1), limits = c(0, 100), name = "% of quartile served") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)),
        fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = .8))) +
  labs(title = paste0("Before vs. after by QUARTILE, WHOLE CATALOGUE (level ", substitutability_level, ", equal weights)"),
       subtitle = "Grey band = full category range; coloured band = this quartile's own range. A tight coloured band inside a wide grey one means this quartile is a narrow slice of a diverse category.",
       x = "normalized goodness (higher = better)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.8), panel.spacing.x = unit(4, "mm"))
```

A few reading notes: a quartile with a wide coloured band contains products
that don't have much in common on this dimension despite being in the same
category — the average for that row is doing more work than it looks. A
narrow coloured band sitting far from the category's grey band means that
quartile is a genuinely distinct, homogeneous slice (e.g. Q1 for a category
where a handful of products are dramatically worse than the rest). Comparing
Q1's arrow length to Q4's directly answers "does the algorithm concentrate its
effort on the worst products in a category, or spread improvement evenly" —
Q1 should generally show the largest movement if it's working as intended,
since those are the products furthest from the gate.


## Gain by dominant dimension — normalized scores {#sec-gainheat}

For each of the 1,771 weight vectors we take the mean gain delivered on each
dimension across all served products, then group the vectors by which dimension
carries the most weight. A well-tailored system puts each row's largest value on
the diagonal.

```{r}
#| label: gain-by-dominant
gain_by_scenario <- cached(
  paste0("gain_by_scenario_", norm_profile, "_", LKEY, "_step", WEIGHT_GRID_STEP),
  c(norm_profile, substitutability_level, WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, POOL_MODE, GATE_THRESHOLD, GATE_MODE), {
  sapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
    nd  <- select_mat_primary[, d]
    del <- matrix(nd[ALT], nrow(ALT), ncol(ALT)) - nd[SRV]
    colMeans(del, na.rm = TRUE)                       # one mean gain per weight vector
  })
})

gain_by_dom <- as.data.frame(gain_by_scenario) %>%
  mutate(dominant_dim = GRID$dominant) %>%
  group_by(dominant_dim) %>%
  summarise(n_scenarios = n(), across(all_of(dim_cols), ~ round(mean(.x), 3)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(dominant_dim = factor(dominant_dim, levels = dim_cols)) %>% arrange(dominant_dim)
save_out(gain_by_dom, "gain_by_dominant_dimension_normalized.csv",
         "Mean normalized gain on each dimension, grouped by the weight vector's dominant dimension.")
show_tbl(gain_by_dom, caption = "Mean normalized gain per dimension, by the scenario's dominant dimension.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-gain-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Mean gain delivered ON each dimension (columns), BY the dominant dimension of the weight vector (rows). Read across each row: the diagonal cell should be the largest."
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 7
gain_by_dom %>% select(dominant_dim, all_of(dim_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-dominant_dim, names_to = "gain_dim", values_to = "val") %>%
  mutate(gain_dim = factor(gain_dim, levels = dim_cols)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(gain_dim, dominant_dim, fill = val)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", val)), size = 3.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7fbff", high = "#08519c", name = "mean gain") +
  labs(title = "Normalized gain by dominant dimension (1,771-weight grid)",
       x = "gain on dimension", y = "scenario's dominant dimension")
```

## Reduction in raw impact — and why the v11 version was wrong {#sec-relgain}

::: {.callout-important appearance="default"}
## The v11 metric was not measurable on this data

v11 computed, per recommendation,
$\text{rel}_d = 100 \times (r_{\text{ref}} - r_{\text{alt}})\, /\, r_{\text{ref}}$
and then averaged. Three independent things break it, and together they produce
exactly the kind of impossible number you spotted (−236% on AW, and values above
+100% on H, which would mean the impact went below zero):

1. **H changes sign.** `H_SS` is the FNS score, which is negative for ~29% of
   products and zero for another ~8%. When $r_{\text{ref}} < 0$ the division
   flips the sign of the whole expression, so a genuine *improvement* is recorded
   as a large negative "reduction". A ratio is simply not defined on an interval
   scale that crosses zero.
2. **AW is zero for 41% of the catalogue.** Every plant-based product has
   `AW_SS = 0`. The guard `abs(r_ref) > 1e-9` silently drops all of them, so the
   AW figure is computed on a *non-random* subsample — only products that contain
   animal input. The near-zero survivors (e.g. 0.46) then generate values like
   −178% from an absolute change that is trivially small.
3. **The ratio is asymmetric and unbounded below.** An improvement can never
   exceed +100%, but a deterioration is unbounded. Halving an impact scores
   +50%; doubling it scores −100%. Averaging such a quantity is systematically
   dragged negative. v11 compounded this by taking the **mean** of the ratios
   *within* each weight scenario before taking the median *across* scenarios, so
   a single pathological product contaminated every scenario and the outer
   median could never wash it out.

**Replacement.** For the three non-negative dimensions (E, AW, SE) we use the
**median fold-change**, computed with the *same offset the normalization uses*,
so zeros are handled identically in the score and in the reported effect:

$$\text{fold}_d=\frac{r_{\text{alt}}+o_d}{r_{\text{ref}}+o_d},\qquad
o_d = \texttt{LOG\_OFFSET\_VALUE}\times \operatorname{median}\!\left(r_d \mid r_d>0\right)$$

then report $100 \times (1 - \operatorname{median}(\text{fold}_d))$. This is
defined for every product (no silent dropping), symmetric in log space, and
robust to the skew. For **H** a ratio is meaningless, so we report the median
change in **FNS points** and the share of swaps that improve the Nutri-Score
letter — both directly interpretable.
:::

```{r}
#| label: relative-impact
RAW_OFFSET <- sapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
  x <- RAW_IMPACT[[d]]; LOG_OFFSET_VALUE * median(x[x > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
})

# Nutri-Score letter as an ordinal grade (A = 5 ... E = 1) for the H read-out.
grade_num <- c(Nutriscore_A = 5, Nutriscore_B = 4, Nutriscore_C = 3,
               Nutriscore_D = 2, Nutriscore_E = 1)[DB$H_nutriscore]

rel_by_scenario <- cached(
  paste0("rel_by_scenario_", norm_profile, "_", LKEY, "_step", WEIGHT_GRID_STEP),
  c(norm_profile, substitutability_level, WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, POOL_MODE, LOG_OFFSET_VALUE, GATE_MODE), {
  out <- list()
  for (d in c("E", "AW", "SE")) {
    r <- RAW_IMPACT[[d]]; o <- RAW_OFFSET[[d]]
    fold <- (matrix(r[ALT], nrow(ALT), ncol(ALT)) + o) / (r[SRV] + o)
    # Geometric mean of the fold change = the multiplicative analogue of the mean.
    # It uses every served product and responds to the whole distribution, while
    # staying symmetric: halving and doubling are equal and opposite in logs.
    out[[paste0("pct_cut_", d)]] <- 100 * (1 - exp(colMeans(log(fold), na.rm = TRUE)))
    # Median fold change: the robustness companion, insensitive to the tails.
    out[[paste0("med_cut_", d)]] <- 100 * (1 - apply(fold, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE))
    # the v11 metric, reproduced for the comparison table below
    naive <- 100 * (r[SRV] - matrix(r[ALT], nrow(ALT), ncol(ALT))) / r[SRV]
    naive[!is.finite(naive)] <- NA_real_
    out[[paste0("v11_mean_", d)]] <- colMeans(naive, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  hs <- RAW_IMPACT[["H"]]
  dH <- hs[SRV] - matrix(hs[ALT], nrow(ALT), ncol(ALT))       # positive = better
  out[["delta_H_points"]] <- colMeans(dH, na.rm = TRUE)
  gg <- matrix(grade_num[ALT], nrow(ALT), ncol(ALT)) - grade_num[SRV]
  out[["pct_H_grade_up"]] <- 100 * colMeans(gg > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  naiveH <- 100 * (hs[SRV] - matrix(hs[ALT], nrow(ALT), ncol(ALT))) / hs[SRV]
  naiveH[!is.finite(naiveH)] <- NA_real_
  out[["v11_mean_H"]] <- colMeans(naiveH, na.rm = TRUE)
  as.data.frame(out)
})

rel_by_dom <- rel_by_scenario %>% mutate(dominant_dim = GRID$dominant) %>%
  group_by(dominant_dim) %>%
  summarise(n_scenarios = n(),
            across(starts_with("pct_cut_"), ~ round(mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
            across(starts_with("med_cut_"), ~ round(mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
            delta_H_points = round(mean(delta_H_points, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            pct_H_grade_up = round(mean(pct_H_grade_up, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(dominant_dim = factor(dominant_dim, levels = dim_cols)) %>% arrange(dominant_dim)
save_out(rel_by_dom, "raw_impact_reduction_by_dominant_dimension.csv",
         "Median % raw-impact reduction (E/AW/SE, offset fold-change) and median FNS-point gain (H), by dominant dimension.")
show_tbl(rel_by_dom, caption = "Corrected raw-impact effect by dominant dimension. E/AW/SE in % impact cut; H in FNS points and % of swaps improving the letter grade.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-relgain-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Median reduction in raw impact for the three non-negative dimensions. Green = impact reduced."
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6.5
rel_by_dom %>% select(dominant_dim, starts_with("pct_cut_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(-dominant_dim, names_to = "gain_dim", values_to = "pct") %>%
  mutate(gain_dim = factor(sub("pct_cut_", "", gain_dim), levels = c("E", "AW", "SE"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(gain_dim, dominant_dim, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct)), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#b2182b", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#1a9850", midpoint = 0,
                       name = "median %\nimpact cut") +
  labs(title = "Median reduction in raw impact, by dominant dimension",
       subtitle = "offset-consistent median fold-change; H is on a separate scale (see table)",
       x = "% reduction on dimension", y = "scenario's dominant dimension")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-relgain-method-comparison
rel_by_scenario %>% mutate(dominant_dim = GRID$dominant) %>% group_by(dominant_dim) %>%
  summarise(`AW: v11 metric`  = round(mean(v11_mean_AW, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            `AW: corrected`   = round(mean(pct_cut_AW,  na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            `H: v11 metric`   = round(mean(v11_mean_H,  na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            `H: corrected (FNS points)` = round(mean(delta_H_points, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  show_tbl(caption = "Old vs. new metric, same runs. The v11 columns are the ones that produce values below -100% or above +100%, which are not attainable for a genuine percentage reduction.")
```

## Variety: distinct alternatives per reference product {#sec-distinct}

Across the 1,771 weight vectors, how many *different* alternatives does a given
reference product end up being pushed towards? A spike at 1 means the
subcategory has a candidate that wins under every possible weighting — no
trade-off exists there, so no tailoring is possible.

```{r}
#| label: fig-distinct-alts
#| fig-cap: "Number of distinct alternatives a reference product receives across the 1,771 theoretical weight vectors."
#| fig-height: 5
distinct_alts <- data.frame(
  row_id       = SRV,
  TH_code      = DB$TH_code[SRV],
  food_product = DB$food_product[SRV],
  SAFAD_L2_cat = ref_cat_vec[SRV],
  n_distinct_alts = apply(ALT, 1, function(r) length(unique(r))),
  top_alt_share   = apply(ALT, 1, function(r) max(table(r)) / length(r)))
save_out(distinct_alts, "distinct_alternatives_per_product.csv",
         "Per served product: number of distinct alternatives and top-alternative share across the weight grid.")

cat(sprintf("Mean distinct alternatives per product: %.2f | median top-alt share: %.1f%% | %.1f%% of products get exactly one alternative under every weighting.\n",
            mean(distinct_alts$n_distinct_alts), 100 * median(distinct_alts$top_alt_share),
            100 * mean(distinct_alts$n_distinct_alts == 1)))

ggplot(distinct_alts, aes(n_distinct_alts)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5, fill = "#4c72b0", colour = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()) +
  labs(title = "Distinct alternatives per reference product across the theoretical weight grid",
       subtitle = paste0("level ", substitutability_level,
                         ", deterministic best-in-pool; a spike at 1 = no trade-off to tailor on"),
       x = "number of distinct alternatives", y = "reference products")
```

## Tailoring per dimension {#sec-tailoring-theory}

The apples-to-apples test. **Within each reference product**, across the 1,771
weight vectors, correlate the weight put on dimension *d* with the score on *d*
of the alternative that gets selected. Then average over reference products,
weighted by nothing in particular since every product sees the same 1,771
vectors.

Doing it within-product is what makes it deconfounded: it never compares across
reference products, so it cannot pick up "certain products sit in pools with
systematically different scores".

```{r}
#| label: tailoring-theoretical
tailoring_grid <- cached(
  paste0("tailoring_grid_", norm_profile, "_", LKEY, "_step", WEIGHT_GRID_STEP),
  c(norm_profile, substitutability_level, WEIGHT_GRID_STEP, POOL_MODE, GATE_MODE), {
  rw <- lapply(dim_cols, function(d) rank(GRID$W[, d]))   # Spearman = Pearson on ranks
  names(rw) <- dim_cols
  res <- sapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
    nd <- select_mat_primary[, d]
    vapply(seq_len(nrow(ALT)), function(i) {
      y <- nd[ALT[i, ]]
      if (length(unique(y)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
      suppressWarnings(cor(rw[[d]], rank(y)))
    }, numeric(1))
  })
  as.data.frame(res)
})

tailoring_summary <- data.frame(
  dimension = dim_cols,
  mean_within_product_spearman = round(sapply(dim_cols, function(d)
    mean(tailoring_grid[[d]], na.rm = TRUE)), 3),
  n_products_with_variation = sapply(dim_cols, function(d) sum(!is.na(tailoring_grid[[d]]))),
  pct_products_positive = round(sapply(dim_cols, function(d)
    100 * mean(tailoring_grid[[d]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)), 1))
save_out(tailoring_summary, "tailoring_per_dimension_theoretical.csv",
         "Within-product Spearman between the weight on d and the selected alternative's score on d, over the weight grid.")
show_tbl(tailoring_summary, caption = "Tailoring per dimension (theoretical weights, within-product Spearman).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tailoring-dist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the within-product tailoring correlation. Mass to the right of zero means putting more weight on a dimension does steer the pick towards that dimension."
#| fig-height: 4.5
tailoring_grid %>% pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "dimension", values_to = "rho") %>%
  filter(!is.na(rho)) %>% mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(rho, dimension, fill = dimension)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = .7, linewidth = .3) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .13, outlier.size = .3, fill = "white", linewidth = .3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Within-product tailoring correlation, per dimension",
       x = "Spearman(weight on d, selected alternative's score on d)", y = NULL)
```

## A worked basket {#sec-basket}

The metrics above are aggregate. This is the concrete version: 22 everyday
products spanning most L1 categories, what the algorithm says about each item,
and the alternatives it pushes most often across the whole weight grid. Items
that clear the gate are shown too — "no change needed" is a legitimate and
frequent output.

```{r}
#| label: basket-table
basket_idx <- match(BASKET_TH, DB$TH_code)
missing_th <- BASKET_TH[is.na(basket_idx)]
if (length(missing_th)) cat("Not in this database, skipped:", paste(missing_th, collapse = ", "), "\n")
basket_idx <- basket_idx[!is.na(basket_idx)]

basket_status <- data.frame(
  TH_code = DB$TH_code[basket_idx], product = DB$food_product[basket_idx],
  subcategory = ref_cat_vec[basket_idx],
  overall = round(overall_primary[basket_idx], 3),
  E = round(select_mat_primary[basket_idx, "E"], 2),
  AW = round(select_mat_primary[basket_idx, "AW"], 2),
  SE = round(select_mat_primary[basket_idx, "SE"], 2),
  H = round(select_mat_primary[basket_idx, "H"], 2),
  status = ELIG[[LKEY]]$reason[basket_idx],
  n_eligible_alternatives = lengths(ELIG[[LKEY]]$cand[basket_idx]))
show_tbl(basket_status, caption = "The basket: objective score, dimension profile, and whether the gate fires.")
```

```{r}
#| label: basket-alternatives
srv_pos <- match(basket_idx, SRV)                 # position within the GRID matrices

# For each (reference, rank) alternative: among the weight vectors that
# actually selected it, which dimension carried the most weight most often?
# Reported as a single dimension, or two joined by "/" when the runner-up is
# within 60% of the leader's count (a genuinely close second, not noise).
dominant_dims_for <- function(idx_wv) {
  tab <- sort(table(GRID$dominant[idx_wv]), decreasing = TRUE)
  if (length(tab) > 1 && tab[2] >= 0.6 * tab[1]) paste(names(tab)[1:2], collapse = " / ") else names(tab)[1]
}

basket_alts_long <- bind_rows(lapply(which(!is.na(srv_pos)), function(j) {
  i <- basket_idx[j]; r <- ALT[srv_pos[j], ]
  tb <- sort(table(r), decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(3, length(unique(r)))]
  alt_ids <- as.integer(names(tb))
  data.frame(
    reference = DB$food_product[i], rank = seq_along(tb),
    alt_product = DB$food_product[alt_ids],
    pct_of_weightings = round(100 * as.numeric(tb) / length(r), 1),
    alt_overall = round(overall_primary[alt_ids], 3),
    overall_gain = round(overall_primary[alt_ids] - overall_primary[i], 3),
    dominant_dims = sapply(alt_ids, function(a) dominant_dims_for(which(r == a))))
}))
save_out(basket_alts_long, "basket_example_alternatives_long.csv",
         "Worked basket: top-3 alternatives per basket item across the 1,771-weight grid, with the dimension(s) most often dominant when each alternative is chosen (long format).")

# Wide format: one row per basket item, one column block (product, % of
# weightings, overall, gain, dominant dimension(s)) per alternative rank.
basket_alts_wide <- basket_alts_long %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = reference, names_from = rank,
              values_from = c(alt_product, pct_of_weightings, alt_overall, overall_gain, dominant_dims),
              names_glue = "alt{rank}_{.value}") %>%
  select(reference,
         alt1_alt_product, alt1_pct_of_weightings, alt1_alt_overall, alt1_overall_gain, alt1_dominant_dims,
         alt2_alt_product, alt2_pct_of_weightings, alt2_alt_overall, alt2_overall_gain, alt2_dominant_dims,
         alt3_alt_product, alt3_pct_of_weightings, alt3_alt_overall, alt3_overall_gain, alt3_dominant_dims) %>%
  setNames(c("reference",
             "Alt 1", "Alt 1: % of weightings", "Alt 1: overall", "Alt 1: gain", "Alt 1: dominant dim(s)",
             "Alt 2", "Alt 2: % of weightings", "Alt 2: overall", "Alt 2: gain", "Alt 2: dominant dim(s)",
             "Alt 3", "Alt 3: % of weightings", "Alt 3: overall", "Alt 3: gain", "Alt 3: dominant dim(s)"))
save_out(basket_alts_wide, "basket_example_alternatives_wide.csv",
         "Worked basket: top-3 alternatives per basket item, one column block per alternative (wide format), including each alternative's most often dominant dimension(s).")
show_tbl(basket_alts_wide, caption = "The three alternatives each gated basket item is most often steered towards, side by side. 'dominant dim(s)' is the weight-vector dimension that was carrying the most weight, most often, among the draws that picked that specific alternative - i.e. the kind of shopper this swap is really for.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-basket
#| fig-cap: "Dimension profile of each gated basket item (grey) and its top 3 most frequently recommended alternatives (shades of green, darkest = most frequent, rank consistent across every panel). Exact % of weightings for each alternative is in the table above; none of the alternatives dominates on every dimension - that is the trade-off the weights arbitrate."
#| fig-height: 22
#| fig-width: 11
basket_profile <- bind_rows(lapply(which(!is.na(srv_pos)), function(j) {
  i <- basket_idx[j]; r <- ALT[srv_pos[j], ]
  tb <- sort(table(r), decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(3, length(unique(r)))]
  top3 <- as.integer(names(tb))
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(item = DB$food_product[i], role = "current product",
               dimension = dim_cols, score = select_mat_primary[i, ]),
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(top3), function(k) data.frame(
      item = DB$food_product[i], role = paste0("alt #", k),
      dimension = dim_cols, score = select_mat_primary[top3[k], ]))))
})) %>% mutate(dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols),
              role = factor(role, levels = c("current product", "alt #1", "alt #2", "alt #3")))

alt_colours <- c("alt #1" = "#1b5e20", "alt #2" = "#4c9a4c", "alt #3" = "#a5d6a7")

ggplot(basket_profile, aes(score, dimension, colour = role, group = role)) +
  geom_line(orientation = "y", linewidth = .5, alpha = .6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ item, ncol = 3, labeller = label_wrap_gen(34)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`current product` = "grey45", alt_colours), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "What the swap actually changes, dimension by dimension",
       x = "normalized goodness (higher = better)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

# Performance under real consumer weights {#sec-consumers}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Run used:** `CONS` — the algorithm run once per survey respondent at level
`r substitutability_level`, randomized with sharpness `r SHARPNESS`, gate and
pool objective. Same battery of metrics as @sec-theoretical, so the two sections
are directly comparable: the only thing that changes is where the weight vectors
come from.
:::

```{r}
#| label: consumer-flag
if (!HAS_CONSUMERS)
  cat("RawData.xlsx not found at", path_xlsx, "- this whole section is skipped.\n")
```

## Consumer weight vectors

Survey points are given on five dimensions. The algorithm has four, so
`points_social` and `points_economy` are averaged into a single socio-economic
weight, then each respondent's four points are normalised to sum to 1.
Respondents with a missing or all-zero answer are dropped (their weights would
be undefined).

```{r}
#| label: consumer-weights
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(readxl))
sheets   <- excel_sheets(here(path_xlsx))
five_pts <- c("points_ecology", "points_social", "points_animalwelfare",
              "points_health", "points_economy")

consumer_raw <- bind_rows(lapply(sheets, function(sh) {
  d <- read_excel(here(path_xlsx), sheet = sh, skip = 1)   # row 1 is a title
  names(d) <- tolower(trimws(names(d)))
  d <- d[, five_pts, drop = FALSE]; d$country <- sh; d
})) %>%
  mutate(points_socioeconomic = (points_social + points_economy) / 2) %>%
  select(points_ecology, points_socioeconomic, points_animalwelfare,
         points_health, country) %>%
  filter(if_all(starts_with("points_"), ~ !is.na(.)))

rs <- rowSums(consumer_raw[, c("points_ecology", "points_socioeconomic",
                               "points_animalwelfare", "points_health")])
consumer_raw <- consumer_raw[rs > 0, ]; rs <- rs[rs > 0]

consumer_weights <- consumer_raw %>%
  mutate(consumer_id = row_number(),
         E = points_ecology / rs, AW = points_animalwelfare / rs,
         SE = points_socioeconomic / rs, H = points_health / rs) %>%
  select(consumer_id, country, all_of(dim_cols))
n_consumer <- nrow(consumer_weights)
W_CONS     <- as.matrix(consumer_weights[, dim_cols])

save_out(consumer_weights, "consumer_weights.csv",
         "Per respondent: country and the four normalised dimension weights.")

consumer_weights %>% mutate(max_w = pmax(E, AW, SE, H)) %>% group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(all_of(dim_cols), ~ round(mean(.x), 3)),
            mean_max_weight = round(mean(max_w), 3), .groups = "drop") %>%
  show_tbl(caption = "Mean respondent weights by country, plus how lopsided the average respondent is (0.25 = perfectly equal).")
```

Real respondents cluster far more tightly than the theoretical grid — country
means sit close to 0.25 on every dimension. That narrow range mechanically
attenuates every correlation in this section relative to @sec-theoretical, even
where the tailoring machinery behaves identically. It is a property of the
survey, not of the algorithm.

## `CONS` — one algorithm run per respondent

```{r}
#| label: build-cons
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
CONS <- cached(
  paste0("CONS_", norm_profile, "_", LKEY, "_n", n_consumer, "_sh", SHARPNESS),
  c(norm_profile, substitutability_level, n_consumer, SHARPNESS, RANDOM_SEED,
    POOL_MODE, GATE_THRESHOLD, file_fp(here(path_xlsx)), GATE_MODE), {
  list(alt = pick_alternatives(ELIG[[LKEY]], select_mat_primary, W_CONS,
                               randomize = TRUE, seed = RANDOM_SEED, sharpness = SHARPNESS),
       served = SRV)
})
ALT_C <- CONS$alt[SRV, , drop = FALSE]        # n_served x n_consumer
cat(sprintf("CONS: %d served products x %d respondents = %.1fM recommendations.\n",
            nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C), length(ALT_C) / 1e6))
```

## Most-recommended alternatives per subcategory

```{r}
#| label: cons-top5
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
cons_top_alts <- data.frame(
    SAFAD_L2_cat = rep(ref_cat_vec[SRV], times = ncol(ALT_C)),
    alt_row_id   = as.vector(ALT_C)) %>%
  count(SAFAD_L2_cat, alt_row_id, name = "times") %>%
  group_by(SAFAD_L2_cat) %>% mutate(share = 100 * times / sum(times)) %>%
  slice_max(times, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>% mutate(rank = row_number()) %>% ungroup() %>%
  transmute(SAFAD_L2_cat, rank, alt_TH_code = DB$TH_code[alt_row_id],
            alt_product = DB$food_product[alt_row_id], times, share = round(share, 1))
save_out(cons_top_alts, "top5_alternatives_by_subcategory_consumers.csv",
         "Top-5 most-recommended alternatives per L2 subcategory across real respondents.")
show_tbl(head(cons_top_alts, 40),
         caption = "Top-5 alternatives per subcategory under real respondent weights (first 40 rows).")
```

### Most-recommended products overall

Same collapse as @sec-top5's grid version, but counted across real respondent
weight vectors instead of the theoretical grid.

```{r}
#| label: cons-top10-overall
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
cons_top10_overall <- data.frame(
    SAFAD_L2_cat = rep(ref_cat_vec[SRV], times = ncol(ALT_C)),
    alt_row_id   = as.vector(ALT_C)) %>%
  count(alt_row_id, name = "times") %>%
  mutate(share = round(100 * times / sum(times), 2)) %>%
  slice_max(times, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  transmute(rank, alt_TH_code = DB$TH_code[alt_row_id], alt_product = DB$food_product[alt_row_id],
            alt_L1_cat = DB$SAFAD_L1_cat[alt_row_id], alt_L2_cat = DB$SAFAD_L2_cat[alt_row_id],
            times, share)
save_out(cons_top10_overall, "top10_alternatives_overall_consumers.csv",
         "Top-10 most-recommended products catalogue-wide, across real respondents.")
show_tbl(cons_top10_overall, caption = "Top-10 most-recommended products overall, across real respondent weights.")
```

## Before vs. after, by dimension and L1 category

Built the same catalogue-wide way as @sec-beforeafter: unserved products
contribute *after = before*, so every L1 category appears.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cons-before-after
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
#| fig-cap: "Mean normalized score before vs. after recommendation across all respondents, among products that actually receive one, by dimension and L1 category. Same served/not-served split as @sec-beforeafter, since the gate and pool are objective and therefore identical for every respondent - only the pick among eligible candidates differs by consumer."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 13
cons_before_after <- bind_rows(lapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
  nd <- select_mat_primary[, d]
  data.frame(L1 = REC$SAFAD_L1_cat[SRV], dimension = d,
             before = nd[SRV],
             after  = rowMeans(matrix(nd[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C)), na.rm = TRUE))
})) %>%
  group_by(dimension, L1) %>%
  summarise(before = mean(before, na.rm = TRUE), after = mean(after, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# L1 categories with zero served products at all (identical set to section 5,
# since gate/pool is objective): before = after = the category's own mean.
cons_before_after <- bind_rows(lapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
  zero_cov <- setdiff(unique(REC$SAFAD_L1_cat), unique(REC$SAFAD_L1_cat[SRV]))
  if (!length(zero_cov)) return(NULL)
  m <- select_mat_primary[, d]
  data.frame(dimension = d, L1 = zero_cov,
             before = sapply(zero_cov, function(cc) mean(m[REC$SAFAD_L1_cat == cc], na.rm = TRUE)))
}), .id = NULL) %>% mutate(after = before) %>% bind_rows(cons_before_after)

cons_before_after <- cons_before_after %>%
  left_join(coverage_L1[, c("L1", "pct_recommended")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(delta = after - before,
         direction = dplyr::case_when(
           pct_recommended == 0 ~ "no recommendations issued",
           delta < -1e-9         ~ "decrease",
           TRUE                  ~ "increase"),
         dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols)) %>%
  left_join(l1_order[, c("L1", "lab")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(l1_order$lab)))

save_out(cons_before_after, "before_after_by_dimension_L1_consumers.csv",
         "Mean normalized score before vs after recommendation per dimension x L1, among served products only, averaged over respondents.")

ggplot(cons_before_after) +
  geom_segment(data = ~ filter(.x, pct_recommended > 0),
               aes(x = before, xend = after, y = lab, yend = lab,
                   colour = direction, alpha = pct_recommended),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = .6) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, pct_recommended == 0),
             aes(before, lab), colour = "grey55", shape = 4, size = 1.6, stroke = .8) +
  geom_point(aes(before, lab), colour = "grey35", size = .9) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(decrease = "#c0392b", increase = "#2e8540",
                                `no recommendations issued` = "grey55"), name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), limits = c(0, 100), name = "% of category served") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  labs(title = "Mean score before vs. after among SERVED products, averaged over real respondents",
       subtitle = "Grey x = category has zero recommendations. Fainter arrow = based on a smaller share of the category.",
       x = "normalized goodness (higher = better)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
```

### The same figure, averaged over the whole catalogue instead

Same caveat as @sec-beforeafter: every product contributes here, so a
category's visible movement is diluted in proportion to `1 - pct_recommended`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cons-before-after-wholecat
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
#| fig-cap: "The same comparison, averaged over the WHOLE catalogue rather than served products only. Unserved products contribute after = before."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 13
cons_before_after_wholecat <- bind_rows(lapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
  nd <- select_mat_primary[, d]
  after <- nd                                    # default: unchanged (unserved)
  after[SRV] <- rowMeans(matrix(nd[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C)), na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(L1 = REC$SAFAD_L1_cat, dimension = d, before = nd, after = after)
})) %>%
  group_by(dimension, L1) %>%
  summarise(before = mean(before, na.rm = TRUE), after = mean(after, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(delta = after - before,
         direction = ifelse(delta < -1e-9, "decrease", "increase or unchanged"),
         dimension = factor(dimension, levels = dim_cols)) %>%
  left_join(l1_order[, c("L1", "lab")], by = "L1") %>%
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(l1_order$lab)))

save_out(cons_before_after_wholecat, "before_after_by_dimension_L1_consumers_whole_catalogue.csv",
         "Mean normalized score before vs after recommendation per dimension x L1, over the WHOLE catalogue, averaged over respondents.")

ggplot(cons_before_after_wholecat) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = before, xend = after, y = lab, yend = lab, colour = direction),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = .5) +
  geom_point(aes(before, lab), colour = "grey35", size = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(decrease = "#c0392b", `increase or unchanged` = "#2e8540"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Mean score before vs. after, WHOLE CATALOGUE, averaged over real respondents",
       subtitle = "Every product contributes; unserved products have after = before by construction.",
       x = "normalized goodness (higher = better)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
```

## Gain by dominant dimension

```{r}
#| label: cons-gain-heatmap
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
cons_dominant <- dim_cols[max.col(W_CONS, ties.method = "first")]
cons_gain <- sapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
  nd <- select_mat_primary[, d]
  colMeans(matrix(nd[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C)) - nd[SRV], na.rm = TRUE)
})
cons_gain_by_dom <- as.data.frame(cons_gain) %>% mutate(dominant_dim = cons_dominant) %>%
  group_by(dominant_dim) %>%
  summarise(n_consumers = n(), across(all_of(dim_cols), ~ round(mean(.x), 3)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(dominant_dim = factor(dominant_dim, levels = dim_cols)) %>% arrange(dominant_dim)
save_out(cons_gain_by_dom, "gain_by_dominant_dimension_consumers.csv",
         "Mean normalized gain per dimension by respondents' dominant dimension.")
show_tbl(cons_gain_by_dom, caption = "Mean normalized gain per dimension, grouped by each respondent's highest-weighted dimension.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cons-gain-heatmap
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
#| fig-cap: "Mean gain delivered ON each dimension, BY respondents' dominant dimension."
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 7
cons_gain_by_dom %>% select(dominant_dim, all_of(dim_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-dominant_dim, names_to = "gain_dim", values_to = "val") %>%
  mutate(gain_dim = factor(gain_dim, levels = dim_cols)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(gain_dim, dominant_dim, fill = val)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", val)), size = 3.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7fbff", high = "#08519c", name = "mean gain") +
  labs(title = "Normalized gain by dominant dimension (real respondents)",
       x = "gain on dimension", y = "respondent's dominant dimension")
```

## Reduction in raw impact

Same corrected metric as @sec-relgain: offset-consistent median fold change for
E/AW/SE, FNS points and grade improvement for H.

```{r}
#| label: cons-relgain
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
cons_rel <- local({
  out <- list()
  for (d in c("E", "AW", "SE")) {
    r <- RAW_IMPACT[[d]]; o <- RAW_OFFSET[[d]]
    fold <- (matrix(r[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C)) + o) / (r[SRV] + o)
    out[[paste0("pct_cut_", d)]] <- 100 * (1 - exp(colMeans(log(fold), na.rm = TRUE)))
  }
  hs <- RAW_IMPACT[["H"]]
  out[["delta_H_points"]] <- colMeans(hs[SRV] - matrix(hs[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C)),
                                      na.rm = TRUE)
  out[["pct_H_grade_up"]] <- 100 * colMeans(
    matrix(grade_num[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C)) - grade_num[SRV] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  as.data.frame(out)
})
cons_rel_by_dom <- cons_rel %>% mutate(dominant_dim = cons_dominant) %>%
  group_by(dominant_dim) %>%
  summarise(n_consumers = n(),
            across(starts_with("pct_cut_"), ~ round(mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
            delta_H_points = round(mean(delta_H_points, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            pct_H_grade_up = round(mean(pct_H_grade_up, na.rm = TRUE), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(dominant_dim = factor(dominant_dim, levels = dim_cols)) %>% arrange(dominant_dim)
save_out(cons_rel_by_dom, "raw_impact_reduction_by_dominant_dimension_consumers.csv",
         "Median % raw-impact reduction and FNS-point gain by respondents' dominant dimension.")
show_tbl(cons_rel_by_dom, caption = "Corrected raw-impact effect by respondents' dominant dimension.")
```

## Variety and tailoring

```{r}
#| label: fig-cons-distinct
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
#| fig-cap: "Distinct alternatives per reference product across respondents. Wider than the theoretical grid because the selection here is randomized (sharpness 15) rather than deterministic."
#| fig-height: 5
cons_distinct <- data.frame(
  row_id = SRV, food_product = DB$food_product[SRV], SAFAD_L2_cat = ref_cat_vec[SRV],
  n_distinct_alts = apply(ALT_C, 1, function(r) length(unique(r))),
  top_alt_share   = apply(ALT_C, 1, function(r) max(table(r)) / length(r)))
save_out(cons_distinct, "distinct_alternatives_per_product_consumers.csv",
         "Per served product: distinct alternatives across respondents.")
cat(sprintf("Mean distinct alternatives per product: %.2f | median top-alt share: %.1f%% | %.1f%% get exactly one.\n",
            mean(cons_distinct$n_distinct_alts), 100 * median(cons_distinct$top_alt_share),
            100 * mean(cons_distinct$n_distinct_alts == 1)))
ggplot(cons_distinct, aes(n_distinct_alts)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5, fill = "#8d6e97", colour = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()) +
  labs(title = "Distinct alternatives per reference product across real respondents",
       x = "number of distinct alternatives", y = "reference products")
```

```{r}
#| label: cons-tailoring
#| eval: !expr HAS_CONSUMERS
# (i) WITHIN-PRODUCT: correlate, for one reference product, each respondent's
#     weight on d against the score on d of the alternative they were shown.
#     Deconfounded and directly comparable to section 5.
# (ii) POOLED: the same correlation over all (product, respondent) pairs at once.
#     Kept only as a contrast -- it mixes in between-product differences, so it
#     is not a clean measure of tailoring.
cons_tailoring <- cached(
  paste0("cons_tailoring_", norm_profile, "_", LKEY, "_n", n_consumer),
  c(norm_profile, substitutability_level, n_consumer, SHARPNESS, RANDOM_SEED), {
  rw <- lapply(dim_cols, function(d) rank(W_CONS[, d])); names(rw) <- dim_cols
  as.data.frame(sapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
    nd <- select_mat_primary[, d]
    vapply(seq_len(nrow(ALT_C)), function(i) {
      y <- nd[ALT_C[i, ]]
      if (length(unique(y)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
      suppressWarnings(cor(rw[[d]], rank(y)))
    }, numeric(1))
  }))
})
pooled_tailoring <- sapply(dim_cols, function(d) {
  nd <- select_mat_primary[, d]
  suppressWarnings(cor(rep(W_CONS[, d], each = nrow(ALT_C)),
                       as.vector(matrix(nd[ALT_C], nrow(ALT_C), ncol(ALT_C))),
                       method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
})
cons_tailoring_summary <- data.frame(
  dimension = dim_cols,
  within_product = round(sapply(dim_cols, function(d) mean(cons_tailoring[[d]], na.rm = TRUE)), 3),
  pooled_confounded = round(as.numeric(pooled_tailoring), 3),
  n_products_with_variation = sapply(dim_cols, function(d) sum(!is.na(cons_tailoring[[d]]))),
  theoretical_grid_reference = tailoring_summary$mean_within_product_spearman)
save_out(cons_tailoring_summary, "tailoring_per_dimension_consumers.csv",
         "Within-product and pooled tailoring correlations for real respondents, next to the theoretical-grid value.")
show_tbl(cons_tailoring_summary,
         caption = "Tailoring per dimension. Compare 'within_product' to the theoretical-grid column: real weights span a much narrower range, which attenuates the correlation even when the mechanism is unchanged.")
```
